title: Evaluation of condensed scalar extensions on w-contractible affines
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], put $R=\Gamma(*,\Lambda)$, and let $T$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $Q\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], put
$$L_T(Q)=\Lambda_T\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline Q\in D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda_T),$$
using ordinary derived tensor in module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], constant sheaves with discrete coefficients, and the canonical constant-section map $\underline R\to\Lambda_T$.

Let $V\to T$ be a pro-etale object with $V=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ w-contractible [sk-def-pe-wlocal]. Thus $A$ is w-strictly local and its connected-component space $S=\pi_0(V)$, with the quotient topology, is an extremally disconnected profinite set (the closure of every open is open). There are natural ring and derived-module isomorphisms
$$\Gamma(V,\Lambda_V)\cong\Gamma(S,\Lambda),\qquad
R\Gamma(V,L_T(Q)|_V)\cong Q\otimes^L_R\Gamma(S,\Lambda).$$
The functor $R\Gamma(V,-):D(V_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda_V)\to D(\Gamma(S,\Lambda))$ is t-exact for the standard t-structures. The displayed comparisons are natural in $Q$. No t-admissibility hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Section 3, equations (3.1), (3.2) and Remark 3.2; Lemma 4.1(1); Proposition 4.3(1), which identifies coefficient sections through the component-site map. The extremal disconnectedness is Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 2.4.8, also explicitly invoked in the proof of Theorem 6.2.

proof.text: Apply the ordinary affine scalar-sections comparison at X=T and at X=Spec A with the identity map. This gives the two coefficient-ring isomorphisms eT and eV, and a natural isomorphism theta between ordinary scalar realization followed by affine sections and extension of module scalars along R to Lambda(pi_0 Spec A).

source.place: Section 3, equation (3.2) and Remark 3.2 in degree zero; Lemma 4.1(1) and Proposition 4.3(1).

proof.text: Evaluation at either affine is additive and exact. The canonical right-derived-functor comparison with the exact induced functor identifies condensedDerivedSections with termwise evaluation. Exact induced functors commute with cohomology, hence preserve both IsLE n and IsGE n. Scalar restriction along eV inverse is exact as well. This proves both t-exactness clauses, independently of scalar extension.

source.place: Section 3, equation (3.2) and Remark 3.2 in degree zero; Lemma 4.1(1) and Proposition 4.3(1).

proof.text: Let c be exact constant module realization on the profinite site, m the prescribed derived-change-of-rings model, and phi the composite of section/internal equivalence, inverse image to T, section-module equivalence, affine evaluation, and scalar transport along eT. All factors of phi are exact. Put H=D(c) followed by m.T and D(phi). Use the exact-localization factorization for c, the actual universal counit of m, the exact-localization factorization for phi, and the chain isomorphism induced by theta to construct a natural transformation beta: Q H to termwise extension of scalars followed by Q. If P is K-flat with flat terms, c(P) is K-flat; m.computes says that its counit is invertible there. Thus beta_P is invertible.

source.place: Section 3, equation (3.2) and Remark 3.2 in degree zero; Lemma 4.1(1) and Proposition 4.3(1).

proof.text: Every unbounded complex of R-modules has a flat-term K-flat resolution. Extension of scalars preserves quasi-isomorphisms between these complexes. Apply the normalized-left-extension theorem to the usual extension/restriction adjunction and this resolving class. It supplies a derived functor E with universal cochain counit epsilon, invertible on every complex in that class, with the independently chosen target localization universe.

source.place: Section 3, equation (3.2) and Remark 3.2 in degree zero; Lemma 4.1(1) and Proposition 4.3(1).

proof.text: The right Kan universal property of (E, epsilon) gives eta:H to E with eta_Q(P) followed by epsilon_P equal to beta_P. Both beta_P and epsilon_P are invertible on flat-term K-flat P, so eta_Q(P) is invertible. For every derived object M choose such a resolution of a cochain preimage; its localized quasi-isomorphism gives Q(P) isomorphic to M. Naturality of eta shows eta_M is invertible, hence eta is a natural isomorphism. The exact-derived composition isomorphisms and the exact right-derived comparison identify H with precisely the displayed condensedScalarRealization/transport/condensedDerivedSections/scalar-restriction composite. Combining this isomorphism with eta proves the derived comparison; the two t-exactness clauses were proved above.
